name: Bithiah
title: Pharaoh's Daughter Who Adopted Moses
summary: Bithiah was a daughter of Pharaoh who found the infant Moses in a basket among the reeds by the Nile and adopted him as her own son. According to Jewish tradition and 1 Chronicles, she was identified as Bithiah, daughter of Pharaoh, who later married Mered from the tribe of Judah. She played a crucial role in God's plan of salvation by saving Moses from death and raising him in the Egyptian court.

keyEvents.title: Finding Moses in the Nile
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh's daughter went down to the Nile to bathe and discovered a basket with a crying baby boy among the reeds. She felt compassion for the child and decided to take him in.

keyEvents.title: Adopting Moses
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh's daughter took the child as her own son and named him Moses, which means "drawn out of water," because she had drawn him out of the water.

keyEvents.title: Arranging a Nurse for Moses
keyEvents.description: Moses' sister Miriam offered to fetch a Hebrew nurse, and Pharaoh's daughter accepted. Thus Moses was nursed by his own biological mother Jochebed.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Bithiah in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles, Bithiah is mentioned as the daughter of Pharaoh and wife of Mered from the tribe of Judah, indicating that she left Egypt and became part of God's people.

keyEvents.title: Moses' faith and choice
keyEvents.description: The book of Hebrews tells us that by faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter when he grew up, choosing instead to suffer with God's people rather than enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.
